title: Air India Plans 50-60 New Planes Per Year Despite Mounting Industry Headwinds
excerpt: The Tata-owned carrier expects deliveries to accelerate from late 2026, with up to 60 aircraft arriving in the next 18 months, even as it grapples with $3 billion in annual losses and airspace restrictions from the Iran conflict.
body:
• Air India Group expects to add 50-60 new aircraft per year for the next seven to eight years, with deliveries accelerating from late 2026 and steady streams from 2027 onward.
  • The airline's order book stands at nearly 600 aircraft — 570 from Airbus and Boeing combined — but fewer than 10% have been delivered so far.
  • Air India faces roughly $3 billion in annual losses, airspace restrictions due to the Iran conflict, record jet fuel prices, and lingering confidence issues from a fatal Boeing 787 crash.

Air India Group is pushing ahead with its massive fleet expansion, planning to add 50 to 60 new aircraft per year for the next seven to eight years despite what its own executives acknowledge as a brutal stretch of industry headwinds, according to Nipun Aggarwal, the airline's chief commercial officer.

Speaking after a panel discussion in Abu Dhabi on July 15, Aggarwal said the carrier expects deliveries to pick up pace from late 2026, with a steady stream of both wide-body and narrow-body aircraft arriving from 2027 onward — roughly 10 to 15 wide-bodies and 45 to 50 narrow-bodies annually.

A Massive Order Book, Slow Delivery

Air India's total order book stands at nearly 600 aircraft. The airline placed a landmark $70 billion order for 470 planes with Airbus and Boeing in 2023, followed by an additional 100 Airbus aircraft in late 2024 — a mix of 90 narrow-body A320 family jets and 10 wide-body A350s.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=6YqLezkVpnM

Yet fewer than 10% of those orders have been delivered. Six A350s are now flying routes including Delhi to London and New York nonstop, but the vast majority of the fleet modernization remains on paper.

"We have been hit by multiple black swan events, which I don't think anybody could have forecasted when we started this transformation journey."

— Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India

The Headwinds

The challenges facing Air India are substantial. Reports citing Bloomberg indicate the carrier has incurred annual losses equivalent to roughly $3 billion. The Iran conflict has forced costly airspace restrictions, Pakistan's airspace closures have disrupted routing, and record jet fuel prices have squeezed margins across the industry.

A fatal Boeing 787 crash has also raised confidence issues that the airline is still working to address. Air India has already cut flights on several routes and is reportedly reevaluating new domestic and international route launches, including plans tied to Noida International Airport.

Some analysts suggest the airline may need to negotiate slower delivery timelines with both Airbus and Boeing to match what the operation and balance sheet can absorb.

Vihaan.AI Transformation

The fleet expansion is the centerpiece of Air India's Vihaan.AI transformation plan, launched after the Tata Group acquired the carrier from the Indian government in January 2022. The five-year plan aims to modernize the fleet, improve operations, and rebuild the airline into a world-class global carrier.

Tata Sons Chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran has described the expansion as essential to meeting India's surging passenger demand. "With India's passenger growth outpacing the rest of the world, its significantly improving infrastructure and an aspirational young population increasingly going global, we see a clear case for Air India to expand," Chandrasekaran said.

What It Means for Diaspora Travelers

For the Indian diaspora in the US and Europe, Air India's fleet renewal directly affects travel quality and options on key routes. The new A350s on the Delhi-New York and Delhi-London routes have already brought a noticeable upgrade in cabin experience. As more aircraft arrive, the airline plans to expand frequencies on high-demand diaspora corridors and add new city pairs.

Air India recently launched Mumbai-Toronto nonstop service, adding 4,400 monthly seats on India-Canada routes, and has doubled down on Australia with premium upgrades and daily flights — routes heavily used by the Indian diaspora.

Despite the headwinds, Aggarwal struck an optimistic tone: "We are very optimistic. It may take a little longer, but we will get there."
